title: Psalm 3: I Laid Me Down and Slept

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 9]

Find your place. Let the covers be heavy and warm. [pause 12]

Tonight we read Psalm 3. The heading says David wrote it when he fled from his own son, Absalom. His family was broken, his city was lost, and he was sleeping in the open. [pause 11]

And still, this psalm has some of the most peaceful words about sleep in the whole Bible. We will read it twice. [pause 14]

verses.text: A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son. LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
I cried unto the LORD with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.
I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.
Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
Salvation belongeth unto the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Lord, how many are my troubles. The psalm starts honest. There are many troubles. Many voices saying there is no help in God. [pause 12]

Then David turns. But you, Lord, are my shield. A shield all around. And the lifter up of my head. [pause 12]

Think of someone gently lifting your chin when you are too tired or too sad to look up. That is the picture. [pause 12]

Then verse five. He lay down, he slept, he woke, because the Lord held him up. In the worst week of his life, David slept. [pause 16]

A companion verse, from the very next psalm. [pause 10]

verses.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.
Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
In peace, lying down and sleeping. Psalm 3 and Psalm 4 sit side by side, like a morning and an evening prayer. [pause 12]

And Psalm 121 tells us the one who keeps Israel never slumbers or sleeps. The proverb speaks of lying down without fear. Someone is keeping watch. [pause 14]

Here is Psalm 3 again. When you reach verse five, let it be yours. [pause 16]

verses.text: A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son. LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
I cried unto the LORD with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.
I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.
Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
Salvation belongeth unto the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will stop here. [pause 8]

Let the room be dark and still around you. Let the pillow be cool. [pause 10]

You have read his words tonight. You can stop thinking about them now and simply rest in them. [pause 12]

Every part of you that is tired, let it be tired. You do not have to be strong right now. [pause 15]

He is awake, so you can sleep. [pause 15]

Let the last words you heard tonight be the ones that stay. Let the rest drift away. [pause 20]

It is all right to stop now. [pause 20]

Rest well. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.6-15.3 minutes.
